chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdallah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:
Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said to some of his companions: Do not do unto others what you would not like to be done unto you; and if someone slaps your right cheek, then give him your left.

key_terms.الخد الأيمن/الأيسر: right/left cheek — the symbolic context of non-retaliation and forbearance
key_terms.لطم: to slap/strike the face — an act of public humiliation in Arab culture
key_terms.ما لا تحب أن يفعل بك: The Golden Rule: do not do to others what you dislike being done to you

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq narrate about the teachings of Jesus on treating others?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a saying of Jesus (Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him) as reported by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). The teaching encapsulates the Golden Rule — do not treat others as you would not wish to be treated — and extends it with an injunction to respond to aggression with forbearance, offering the left cheek when struck on the right. This saying parallels Sermon on the Mount teachings and illustrates the shared ethical heritage of the Abrahamic prophets in Shia tradition.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab from `Ali b. Asbat from his uncle Ya`qub b. Salim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as):
`Isa b. Maryam (a.s.) said to some of his companions: Do not do unto others what you would not like to be done unto you. If someone slaps your right cheek, then give him your left.
